Familiarity with ticketing and IT service management systems. Good troubleshooting and problem-solving skills. Ability to analyze logs, alerts, and network events. review_candidates.title: Senior Infrastructure & Cloud Engineer (IaaS)
review_candidates.description: Overview Looking to make a difference and help modernize critical government missions? Join Acuity's team supporting the U.S. Department of State. As a Senior Infrastructure & Cloud Engineer (IaaS), you will provide hands-on engineering support for mission-critical data center, virtualization, compute, storage, hybrid-cloud, and globally distributed infrastructure. This role is deeply focused on enterprise VMware environments, Windows Server and Linux platforms, hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI), SAN/NAS storage, and the resilient infrastructure services that support Department of State operations worldwide. Working closely with the Cloud Technical Lead, Cloud Engineers, Automation Engineers, Network Engineers, Cybersecurity teams, and government stakeholders, you will provide Tier 3 infrastructure engineering and troubleshooting, support infrastructure lifecycle modernization, and ensure the availability, security, resiliency, capacity, and performance of enterprise systems across domestic, overseas, on-premises, and cloud environments. Why Acuity? Are you ready to use your expertise in the areas of IT Modernization, Data Enablement, and Hyperautomation to make a real difference? Join Acuity, Inc., a technology consulting firm that supports federal agencies. We combine industry partnerships and long-term federal experience with innovative technical leadership to support our customers’ critical missions. Responsibilities Design, deploy, administer, and maintain enterprise data center, compute, virtualization, storage, HCI, operating system, and hybrid-cloud infrastructure supporting mission-critical operations. Provide significant hands-on administration and engineering support for enterprise VMware environments, including VMware ESXi, vCenter, clusters, virtual networking, resource management, upgrades, patching, and lifecycle activities. Deploy, configure, administer, patch, harden, and troubleshoot Windows Server and Linux operating systems supporting enterprise applications and infrastructure services. Engineer and support enterprise compute and hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI), including integration with virtualization, networking, storage, backup, and disaster recovery services. Administer and troubleshoot enterprise SAN/NAS storage platforms and virtualization-storage integrations, including capacity, performance, availability, connectivity, and lifecycle considerations. Provide Tier 3 infrastructure troubleshooting and root cause analysis for complex issues spanning servers, virtualization, storage, operating systems, cloud services, and dependent infrastructure components. Design, implement, test, and maintain high-availability, disaster recovery, backup, resiliency, and business-continuity capabilities for mission-critical infrastructure. Plan and execute infrastructure lifecycle activities, including technology refresh, patching, upgrades, migrations, and remediation of end-of-life (EOL) and end-of-support (EOS) hardware and software. Monitor infrastructure health, availability, capacity, and performance using enterprise monitoring and observability platforms; identify trends, constraints, and opportunities for proactive remediation and optimization. Use PowerShell, Bash, Python, Ansible, Terraform, or similar technologies to automate infrastructure provisioning, configuration, administration, compliance, and repetitive operational tasks. Support Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) and hybrid-cloud environments using at least one major cloud service provider such as AWS or Microsoft Azure, including integration between cloud and on-premises infrastructure. Support overseas and globally distributed infrastructure deployments and coordinate with geographically dispersed or remote teams to maintain consistent, reliable infrastructure services across locations and time zones. Operate within established ITSM disciplines, including change, incident, problem, configuration, and release management; participate in root cause analysis and continuous service improvement. Partner with Cybersecurity teams to implement federal security and configuration requirements, including system hardening, vulnerability remediation, secure baselines, STIG-aligned controls, NIST/RMF compliance, and continuous monitoring. Collaborate with Cloud and Automation Engineers to implement Infrastructure as Code (IaC), configuration management, standardized deployment patterns, and infrastructure modernization while maintaining operational stability. Develop and maintain technical documentation, infrastructure diagrams, configuration standards, runbooks, operational procedures, and lifecycle roadmaps. Perform additional duties as assigned in support of customer mission objectives. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience. Minimum of eight (8) years of experience supporting enterprise infrastructure, systems engineering, data center operations, or Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) environments. Significant hands-on enterprise VMware experience, including VMware ESXi and vCenter administration, troubleshooting, patching/upgrades, cluster management, and virtualization lifecycle support. Strong hands-on experience administering and troubleshooting both Windows Server and Linux operating systems in enterprise environments. Experience supporting enterprise compute and hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI) platforms in highly available production environments. Experience administering enterprise SAN and/or NAS storage and supporting storage integration with virtualized infrastructure. Demonstrated Tier 3 infrastructure troubleshooting and root cause analysis experience across compute, virtualization, storage, operating systems, and related infrastructure services. Experience designing, implementing, or supporting high availability, disaster recovery, backup, resiliency, and business-continuity solutions. Experience managing infrastructure lifecycle activities, including upgrades, migrations, technology refresh, and EOL/EOS remediation. Experience with enterprise infrastructure monitoring, capacity management, performance analysis, and availability management. Hands-on scripting or automation experience using PowerShell, Bash, Python, Ansible, Terraform, or similar technologies. Experience supporting at least one major cloud service provider (AWS or Microsoft Azure) and hybrid-cloud integration with enterprise on-premises infrastructure. Experience working within ITSM processes and disciplines, including change management, incident management, problem management, and root cause analysis. Experience implementing federal security and configuration compliance requirements, such as NIST RMF, NIST SP 800-53, FISMA, STIGs, vulnerability remediation, system hardening, or comparable federal standards. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, documentation, communication, and cross-team collaboration skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting globally distributed, overseas, or remote enterprise infrastructure environments, particularly environments requiring coordination across geographically dispersed teams. VMware Certified Professional (VCP) or equivalent VMware certification. Experience with enterprise HCI platforms such as VMware vSAN/VxRail, Nutanix, or comparable technologies. Experience with enterprise storage technologies and vendors supporting SAN/NAS, backup, replication, and disaster recovery. AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate or Professional, Microsoft Azure Administrator Associate, or comparable cloud certification. Red Hat Certified System Administrator (RHCSA), Red Hat Certified Engineer (RHCE), Microsoft server certification, or comparable operating system certification. Experience supporting the U.S. Department of State or other federal civilian agencies. Experience with enterprise monitoring, observability, capacity, and performance-management platforms. Experience with Kubernetes, Docker, OpenShift, or related enterprise container technologies. Familiarity with Zero Trust principles and secure hybrid-cloud infrastructure architectures. Clearance Requirement Active Secret or Top Secret security clearance required. Min USD $145,000.00/Yr. Max USD $195,000.00/Yr. Salary Range The salary range for this position represents Acuity's good faith estimate of the compensation for this job title at the time of posting. Final compensation will be determined based on factors including, but not limited to, the candidate's qualifications, experience, education, certifications, skills, geographic location, contract requirements, applicable labor categories, and, where applicable, contract award and funding.

review_candidates.title: Network Operations Center Manager - Glomfjord
review_candidates.description: Please note: This role requires you to live and work in or near Glomfjord. We currently cannot sponsor visas but can support EU citizens relocating. About Nscale At Nscale, we are building the infrastructure for Europe’s AI revolution. Nscale are developing cutting-edge sovereign generative AI solutions, powered by a new generation of high-performance, sustainable data centres and GPUs built specifically for AI workloads. The growth of artificial intelligence is driving unprecedented global demand for compute and GPU infrastructure. Nscale is positioned at the heart of this transformation — building platforms that will enable the next decade of innovation. Nscale are working closely with the world’s most advanced AI technology providers, integrating next-gen compute hardware and GPU clusters in both partner and Nscale built facilities. This is an opportunity to join Nscale’s journey, play a key role in delivering transformative AI infrastructure, and help shape a company designed to scale rapidly across Europe and beyond. About The Role We are seeking a highly skilled and resilient Network Operations Center (NOC) Manager to lead our critical infrastructure monitoring and incident response teams at our data center in Glomfjord. Taking advantage of the region's green energy and cool climate, our facility requires top-tier operational oversight. As the NOC Manager, you will be the guardian of our network's uptime, stability, and security. You will oversee a 24/7/365 team of engineers and technicians, ensuring that system anomalies are detected instantly, communicated clearly, and resolved rapidly. This role balances strategic leadership—driving process improvements and automation—with hands-on technical guidance during high-pressure incidents. What You'll Be Doing People Leadership & Team Management: Lead, develop, and manage a 24/7/365 Network Operations Centre team, including recruitment, onboarding, training, performance management, coaching, and career development. Create shift schedules that ensure continuous operational coverage while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous learning, customer focus, and operational excellence. Operational Management: Oversee the day-to-day operation of the NOC, ensuring the continuous monitoring of network infrastructure, servers, customer environments, Building Management Systems (BMS), and critical data centre infrastructure. Ensure operational procedures are consistently followed and service levels are maintained. Incident & Major Incident Management: Act as the primary operational escalation point for critical (Tier 3+) network, infrastructure, and facility-related incidents. Lead major incident response activities, coordinate cross-functional teams, perform root cause analysis (RCA), facilitate post-incident reviews, and ensure corrective and preventative actions are implemented to minimise repeat occurrences. Building Management System (BMS) Oversight: Ensure effective monitoring and operational oversight of the Building Management System, including electrical distribution, UPS systems, generators, HVAC, CRAC/CRAH units, environmental monitoring, leak detection, fire detection, and access control systems. Review critical alarms, validate escalation processes, monitor infrastructure health, and ensure facility-related issues are resolved in accordance with operational procedures. Environmental & Infrastructure Reporting: Monitor environmental performance across the data centre, including temperature, humidity, cooling efficiency, power utilisation, and other critical infrastructure metrics. Produce operational reports highlighting trends, risks, recurring alarms, and recommendations for improving facility reliability and operational resilience. SLA, KPI & Performance Management: Monitor, analyse, and report on key operational performance indicators including uptime, incident response times, ticket resolution, alarm response, environmental compliance, customer SLAs, and NOC productivity. Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly operational reports for management, identifying trends and opportunities for continual improvement. Process & Operational Governance: Develop, maintain, enforce, and continuously improve the NOC's Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), operational runbooks, monitoring standards, escalation procedures, and incident response workflows. Ensure all operational documentation remains current and aligned with industry best practices. Vendor & Facilities Coordination: Coordinate with on-site Data Centre Operations, Facilities teams, Mechanical and Electrical engineers, Security personnel, and external vendors regarding planned maintenance, infrastructure upgrades, and emergency works affecting network or facility operations. Ensure maintenance activities are appropriately planned, monitored, communicated, and documented. Shift Operations & Handover Management: Ensure comprehensive operational handovers between shifts, including active incidents, BMS alarms, maintenance activities, operational risks, customer-impacting events, and outstanding actions. Maintain high standards of communication to ensure seamless continuity of operations. Continuous Improvement & Automation: Identify opportunities to improve monitoring capabilities, automate routine operational tasks, reduce false alarms, streamline workflows, and enhance overall operational efficiency. Work closely with Engineering teams to implement improvements to monitoring platforms, reporting, and operational tooling. Risk, Compliance & Business Continuity: Ensure all NOC operations comply with company policies, customer contractual obligations, health and safety requirements, and applicable industry standards. Support business continuity planning, disaster recovery exercises, operational audits, and customer compliance reviews while proactively identifying and mitigating operational risks. About You Experience & Education Proven Leadership: 4+ years of experience managing or leading a team within a NOC, Technical Assistance Center (TAC), or critical data center environment. Technical Background: 6+ years of hands-on experience in network engineering, systems administration, or infrastructure operations. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Network Engineering, Information Technology, or equivalent practical experience. Technical Skills Networking Expertise: Deep understanding of routing protocols (BGP, OSPF), switching, firewalls, VPNs, and load balancing. Certifications (Highly Desirable): CCNP/CCIE, Juniper JNCIP/JNCIE, ITIL Foundation or higher, or relevant cloud/Linux certifications. Monitoring & Systems: Strong proficiency with enterprise-level monitoring, SIEM, and ticketing tools (e.g., Jira Service Management, ServiceNow). Environment Familiarity: Understanding of data center physical infrastructure (UPS, cooling systems, power distribution) is a major plus. Soft Skills & Core Traits Calm Under Pressure: Ability to maintain focus, think logically, and lead a team effectively during high-severity outages. Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills in English (Norwegian language skills are a strong asset for local coordination). Willingness to be site-based in Norway. Problem Solver: A data-driven mindset with a passion for troubleshooting complex, multi-layered technical challenges. What We Can Offer You You’ll have the opportunity to help shape the operating standards behind a next-generation AI cloud platform, working on complex infrastructure challenges with real ownership and impact. This is a chance to play a meaningful role in scaling high-performance, sustainable data centre operations in a fast-moving environment. Equal Opportunities Statement We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds. If there’s anything we can do to accommodate your specific situation, please let us know. The responsibilities outlined in this job description are not exhaustive and are intended to provide a general overview of the position. The employee may be required to perform additional duties, tasks, and responsibilities as assigned by management, consistent with the skills and qualifications required for the role.
